purpose: Introduce a first-class bounded incident-repair lifecycle and reconcile construction lifecycle ownership so governance-only and already-merged defect repairs do not impersonate forward product selection or require routine meta-governance mutation.

lineage.outcome: Post-merge or governance defects can be repaired under one exact incident-bound authority without inventing a product node, reopening completed work, or allowing new product construction to masquerade as repair.
lineage.capability: Bounded incident-repair lifecycle and lifecycle-owner reconciliation

why_now: PR #211 repaired the trusted Steward bootstrap and was post-merge verified, but first use exposed two governance mismatches: already-merged/governance repairs cannot always bind a dependency-ready product node (#247), and ordinary governance incorrectly requires the immutable automation registry to mirror current construction lifecycle (#248). Qualification also exposed closure/event-stream, exact-path and test-isolation obligations that belong to the same governance repair because they are necessary for the new lifecycle to terminate truthfully, remain bounded and stay portable across the required platform matrix.

implementation_contract.exclusive_mode: ACTIVE authority is either normal completion-graph construction or INCIDENT-REPAIR, never both.
implementation_contract.governance_repair: For a GOVERNANCE incident repair, allowed_exact_paths must equal the observed changed-file set exactly, allowed_prefixes must be empty, product_code_allowed must be false, and every changed file must remain inside governance/**, tests/governance/**, or the exact trusted Steward workflow path. Missing and unused surplus path authority both fail closed.
implementation_contract.merged_product_repair: For a MERGED_PRODUCT incident repair, allowed_exact_paths must also equal the observed changed-file set exactly and allowed_prefixes must be empty. The repair additionally requires an exact target merge that predates incident discovery, every construction-sensitive changed path must be explicitly enumerated, and every such construction path must already exist at that target merge. Missing, broad-prefix and unused surplus authority all fail closed.
implementation_contract.incident_truth: An ACTIVE incident repair names currently open repairable durable incidents through incident_repair_ids. incidents.jsonl is append-only event history and current incident truth is the latest row for each durable incident ID. An INACTIVE receipt carries no active incident_repair_ids; exact terminal lineage is inert closure evidence through closed_incident_repair_ids plus closed_repair_receipt_id. closed_incident_repair_ids identify the governing incident authority consumed by the closed bounded repair; they do not by themselves assert that the parent incident is resolved. Terminal closure requires an exact evidence-bound repair-completion event for each governing incident. If the parent incident still has obligations, its latest event remains OPEN, carries repair_completed_at, a non-empty repair_completion_condition, non-empty remaining_open_obligations, the preserved repair_contract, and exact ACTIVE/closure receipt bindings. Only when the full incident closure contract is actually satisfied may the latest event be RESOLVED with resolved_at and resolution_condition. Thus #247/#248 may close after integration while parent incident #206 remains OPEN for its remaining repair ledger.
implementation_contract.runtime_truth: governance/current_state.json owns construction lifecycle. automation_registry.json remains declarative actor/authority bounds and is not a live runtime-state source. Runtime handoff derives current open incidents from the latest event per incident ID.
implementation_contract.trust: Lifecycle enforcement surfaces are protected behind explicit meta-governance reopen, including ordinary governance, incident-repair authority, context lifecycle, supervision, runtime handoff, Steward integration checking and staged consumer smoke. The pull_request_target workflow uses the trusted base copy; this bootstrap PR therefore also requires substantive manual review of the newly introduced helper before it can become base-owned for later PRs. The construction controller's authority, parent and allowed_mutations remain trusted registry fields and ordinary PR mutation is directly regression-tested to fail through the base-owned Steward boundary.

completion_proof: normal ACTIVE construction remains graph-node/dependency bound and is not retyped as incident repair by the specialized helper
a valid normal ACTIVE product receipt passes without mutating the declarative automation registry lifecycle state
GOVERNANCE repair passes with zero ACTIVE graph nodes and unchanged declarative automation lifecycle projection
GOVERNANCE repair rejects broad allowed path prefixes, missing exact paths, and unused surplus exact paths; allowed_exact_paths equals the observed changed-file set
MERGED_PRODUCT repair rejects broad allowed path prefixes, missing exact paths and unused surplus exact paths; allowed_exact_paths equals the observed changed-file set
MERGED_PRODUCT repair additionally requires a pre-incident target merge and pre-existing repaired construction paths
construction-controller authority, parent and allowed_mutations mutations are rejected in an ordinary PR by the trusted automation-registry boundary

INACTIVE receipts cannot carry active incident_repair_ids; terminal closure preserves inert closed_incident_repair_ids and closed_repair_receipt_id bound to the exact prior ACTIVE repair without implying that a still-open parent incident is resolved
append-only incident history permits repeated incident IDs while other durable JSONL registries retain unique IDs

current open-incident projections use the latest event per incident ID so an evidence-bound OPEN_REPAIR_COMPLETED event can close one bounded repair while preserving parent incident authority for the next repair

a still-open parent repair-completion event must preserve exact ACTIVE/closure receipt bindings, evidence, repair_completed_at, repair_completion_condition, remaining_open_obligations and repair_contract

a naked RESOLVED label cannot close a repair: true incident resolution still requires evidence, resolution condition, resolved_at, exact ACTIVE repair receipt binding, and exact terminal closure receipt binding
new product files cannot be introduced through MERGED_PRODUCT repair mode
protected lifecycle enforcement surfaces cannot be changed by an ordinary PR without explicit meta-governance reopen
automation registry cannot reclaim runtime lifecycle ownership
governance-test Git maintenance suppression is scoped to governance tests and does not alter product/runtime Git policy
exact-head governance, full regression and staged consumer smoke pass on Linux, Windows and macOS
substantive exact-head review is terminal before merge
next_selection_rule: After this governance repair is merged and post-merge verified, close this exact ACTIVE repair receipt through inert evidence-bound closure lineage while preserving #206 as OPEN with its remaining obligations; then select the next bounded #206 repair. Close #206 only after its full repair/verification contract is actually satisfied.
